title: Trustworthy Autonomy
description: Nine principles for systems that deserve the authority we give them. A field guide to evidence, boundaries, and learning from consequences.

title: Verdicts require Epistemics
description: An autonomous agent investigates 5XX errors—and learns to separate what it observes, what it believes, and what it can safely do next.

title: Evidence requires Provenance
description: A precise number can tell the wrong story. Follow a claim back through the query, the cohort, and everything the summary left out.

title: State requires Ownership
description: The human paused the rollout. A late agent report says it is running. Which version of reality gets to win?

title: Autonomy requires a Dial
description: One agent can investigate freely, prepare a rollback, and still need permission to execute it. Authority belongs to the action.

title: Inputs require a Trust Boundary
description: A log line says the deployment is pre-approved. How does the system keep an observation from becoming an order?

title: Knowledge requires a Clock
description: The dashboard is accurate. It is also describing a world that has already changed. Truth needs a time boundary.

title: Delegation requires Ceilings
description: Every helper makes a reasonable request. Together, they overwhelm the system they came to investigate.

title: Failure requires a Ladder
description: When the agent loses its instruments, what should it give up first? Design the descent before the incident.

title: Learning requires Outcomes
description: The rollout looked healthy at thirty minutes. Four hours later, a queue filled. Who goes back and grades the earlier verdict?

title: Engineering Autonomous Agents
description: Connecting intelligence, purpose, and action in systems we can depend on.

title: Judgment Under Uncertainty
description: How should an autonomous system act when its understanding is incomplete?

title: What does “good” mean for an agent?
description: Quality begins with a shared understanding of what matters.

title: Skills aren’t policies
description: Knowing how to act and having the authority to act are different things.

title: Memory should accumulate judgment
description: Experience becomes useful when it improves the next decision.

title: Context engineering vs. harness engineering
description: Understanding the world and acting within it are connected engineering problems.

title: Why agent verifiers fail
description: Agreement is more useful when it comes from independent perspectives.

title: Focus
description: Engineering autonomous agents, embedding trustworthiness, and learning from experience.

title: Principles
description: Nine principles of trustworthy autonomy: epistemics, provenance, ownership, authority, trust boundaries, time, delegation, failure, and outcomes.

title: Ideas in progress
description: Open questions about autonomy, trust, learning, and human judgment.

title: About
description: About Chaitanya and Oddly.
